h1: The Twin Lotus Hotel Nakhon Si Thammarat — the big downtown hotel where service is still the real selling point
intro: When locals think of a large hotel in downtown Nakhon Si Thammarat, The Twin Lotus Hotel is one of the first names that comes up · It's a high-rise on Phatthanakan Khukhwang Road that has been open since 1995 and had a major renovation in 2016 · This is not a sleek new boutique stay, but a large 4-star hotel with 390-plus rooms, an outdoor pool, spa, gym, free parking and an airport shuttle — from around ฿800/night · Real guest reviews agree on the warm staff and good value, with the trade-off being the dated feel of parts of the building.

body.html: The Twin Lotus Hotel has been operating since 1995 and is one of the most familiar high-rises to Nakhon Si Thammarat residents · It sits on Phatthanakan Khukhwang Road in Nai Mueang, across from Lotus and a short drive from Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, the heart of the city · A major renovation in 2016 freshened parts of it, but the overall feel is still that of an older hotel · This is not a design-led boutique stay — it is a large 4-star hotel with 390-plus rooms that does its job well, with full facilities for both tourists and people here for work.

Rooms range from Standard and Superior Twin/Double (around 32 sqm) up to Junior and Executive Suites · What guests mention often is that rooms are more spacious than expected, with large beds, good sleep, and nice city views from the higher floors · Higher-floor rooms, especially the renovated ones, look noticeably newer and more comfortable · The trade-off is that furniture and bathrooms on the older floors keep their original style, and some rooms lack a minibar or tea/coffee set — if you need those, ask when booking.

"Booked it because it was cheap, but got more than I expected — spacious room, soft bed, smiling staff who helped with everything, and a breakfast with local Southern khanom jeen and khao yam that was really tasty."

The thing guests praise most consistently is the staff service · "Friendly, helpful, attentive staff" appears on almost every review page — it's the main reason the overall score reaches 9.2 · The outdoor pool is praised as clean and pleasant, and the gym is better-equipped than you'd expect for a provincial hotel · There's a spa, sauna, two restaurants and a large conference centre · Breakfast is a buffet praised for its local dishes, especially khanom jeen with curry sauce and Southern khao yam, while Western options are present but not the highlight.

Location is the main reason people choose it · It's central, on Phatthanakan Khukhwang Road across from Lotus, within walking distance for shopping · It's a convenient base for visiting Wat Phra Mahathat, for official or business travel, or as a stopover before heading on to Khanom, Sichon or Khiriwong · The hotel offers an airport shuttle (the airport is about 15–20 minutes away) and ample free parking, which matters a lot if you're driving yourself · The city's well-known curry-rice shops and old-style coffee houses are only a short drive into the old-town area.

To be honest, per real guest sentiment: The Twin Lotus is an older property that is well looked after, but not every floor is in the same condition · Some reviews mention dated bathrooms and furniture on lower floors, very cold air-con in the lobby and restaurant, and limited Western breakfast choices · If you want a newer-looking room, ask for a renovated higher-floor room when booking — reviews say staff are happy to oblige where availability allows · Guests who are disappointed usually expected a brand-new 4-star standard, while those who understand they're booking a long-running, service-focused city hotel tend to be satisfied.

In short, if you want a large downtown Nakhon Si Thammarat hotel with a pool, gym, free parking, airport shuttle, a central location across from the mall, and genuinely warm service — The Twin Lotus delivers, at a price that's good value · Its 9.2 score from 173 Trip.com reviews and top ranking in the city capture it accurately: "good service, spacious rooms, good value" · It works well both as a central place to stay and as a base for exploring the wider province.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a renovated higher-floor room facing the city when booking or at check-in — these look noticeably newer and have better views · And don't skip the Southern-Thai breakfast, especially khanom jeen with curry sauce and khao yam — the breakfast locals actually eat, and better value than hunting for Western options on the buffet.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Twin Lotus Hotel Nakhon Si Thammarat

faq.q: Where is The Twin Lotus Hotel in Nakhon Si Thammarat, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The Twin Lotus Hotel is at 97/8 Phatthanakan Khukhwang Road, Nai Mueang, in downtown Nakhon Si Thammarat · It's across the road from Lotus · It's about a 10-minute drive to Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan and the old town, roughly 15–20 minutes from Nakhon Si Thammarat Airport (NST), and about 40 minutes to Khiriwong / Lan Saka.

faq.q: How much does The Twin Lotus Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿800/night for a Standard Twin (~32 sqm) · A Superior Double runs about ฿950, a Deluxe Twin around ฿1,100, and a Junior Suite around ฿1,600 · Prices vary by date and platform — compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Is The Twin Lotus Hotel old? Are the rooms clean?
faq.a: It opened in 1995 and was renovated in 2016, so the building still feels of its era · Most reviews praise the rooms as clean and spacious, with large, comfortable beds and excellent service · The caveat is that room condition varies by floor and older-floor rooms keep their original style, so ask for a renovated higher-floor room.

faq.q: Who is The Twin Lotus Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for travellers who want a large, good-value downtown hotel with strong service in Nakhon Si Thammarat · Good for visiting Wat Phra Mahathat, for official or business travel, and for families wanting a pool and free parking · It's a handy base before continuing to Khanom, Sichon or Khiriwong · It's not for those after a modern boutique design hotel.

faq.q: Does The Twin Lotus Hotel have a pool and airport shuttle?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor pool that reviews praise as clean and pleasant, plus a gym, spa and sauna · It offers an airport shuttle (about 15–20 minutes) you can arrange in advance, and ample free parking for those driving themselves.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at The Twin Lotus Hotel?
faq.a: Breakfast is a buffet whose highlight is the Southern-Thai dishes, especially khanom jeen with curry sauce and khao yam, which reviews praise as tasty and varied · Western options are available but not the highlight — if you want a full Western breakfast you may find the choice limited.
